clue.text: Child's play for shepherdess in nursery

definitions.meaning: the hide-and-reveal game played with babies, the same as peekaboo
the girl in the nursery rhyme who lost her sheep

explanation.surface: A nursery-school play in which a child takes the part of a shepherdess.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is the peekaboo game played with infants; the second is the sheep-losing girl of the familiar nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Shake some cereal on to bowl

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: bran is a type of cereal husk
a dish is a bowl

explanation.surface: Sprinkling some cereal into a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: To wave something about threateningly is to flourish or shake it, as with a sword.

clue.text: Dream lover takes drink, holding girl up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
the drink word holds the girl's name within it

parts.note: to sup is to drink
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A dreamy suitor has a drink while lifting his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dream is Shakespeare's 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', whose players act the tragic lover Pyramus. 'holding' puts MARY in SUP; 'up' reverses SUMARYP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyramus, Thisbe's lover, is played by Bottom in the mechanicals' play within Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Dear old husband, possibly, rather thoughtful

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, a husband being one example
pensive means deep in thought

explanation.surface: Someone describes their former husband as a dear and rather thoughtful man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like an affectionate address but means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dear costs a lot of money, so it is costly.

clue.text: A female Liberal, say, in excited state

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal in British politics
to say something is to utter it

explanation.surface: A woman from the Liberal party gets worked up over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a flutter is an idiom for nervous agitation, so the word describes someone excited and jittery.

clue.text: Deal with paper that carries campaign messages

parts.note: to field a question is to deal with it
the Telegraph is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: Handling a newspaper that reports on a political campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Telegraph is a British national newspaper. 'campaign' here is military, not political.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable signalling system used by armies in war sent orders and reports across a battle zone.

clue.text: Remove block after Scots poet has been beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the poet's name loses its first letter

parts.note: William Dunbar was a Scottish poet of the fifteenth century

explanation.surface: Clearing an obstruction after a Scottish poet was executed.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns is the poet most solvers reach for first, but no beheading of it fits; the poet is Dunbar. 'after' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To take away the bar fastening a door is to unblock it.

clue.text: Isn't it common to go up and hug a queen?

indicators.note: the slang phrase wraps around the single letter
in a down clue, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: ain't it is the uneducated form of isn't it

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is vulgar to rush up and embrace a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' means vulgar speech, AIN'T IT. 'hug' puts A inside that, giving AINATIT, and 'to go up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy queen of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream', Oberon's consort, is the royal meant.

clue.text: He may be calling for a double

definitions.meaning: a bell-... calls the changes, or one who telephones
a dead ... is someone's exact double

explanation.surface: A man phoning to ask for a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person who sounds bells or rings a phone; the other is a lookalike, as in the idiom 'dead ringer'.

clue.text: After going on demo, demands for one's dismissal

indicators.note: the demands come after the marching in the answer

parts.note: marching is what protesters do on a demo
orders are demands or commands

explanation.surface: After joining a protest, someone is sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: To be given one's notice to leave a job is idiomatically being told to march off.

clue.text: Fighter, perhaps, rejected opening, in a way

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the phrase for 'a way'

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or way

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the word for an opening is read in reverse

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin

explanation.surface: A boxer turned down a chance in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' is the reversal signal and 'in' the container signal. 'Fighter, perhaps' defines by example, which is why 'perhaps' is there; the fighter is a plane, not a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter is one kind of military aircraft, so the general flying machine is defined by example.

clue.text: Fail to declare weapon to police

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a side that does not declare its innings closed carries on batting
the truncheon a police officer carries

explanation.surface: Someone smuggling a gun past customs without declaring it to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a captain may 'declare', ending the side's innings early; not doing so means the batsmen bat on.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is the cricket phrase for continuing to bat; as one word it is a police officer's stick.

clue.text: March almost pleasant? No, quite diabolical

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: nice is a synonym of pleasant

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the March weather is fairly mild and is told it has been dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is a protest demonstration, DEMO; 'almost' cuts NICE to NIC. 'No,' merely links the surface question to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fiendish enough to come from a devil is as wicked as can be, matching thoroughly diabolical.

clue.text: Disturb king, in peril after loss of rook

indicators.note: the royal abbreviation is placed inside the shortened word for peril
the word for peril is used once a letter has been lost from it

parts.note: danger is a synonym of peril
R is the chess notation for a rook
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A chess player rattles their opponent's king, which is in danger now a rook has been taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after loss of' drops the rook from the word for peril, and 'in' places the king inside what is left. ER is more often the Queen, but Edward Rex makes it a king too.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle or throw into disorder is to disturb, particularly the mind, as with a person driven mad.

clue.text: Dish of oriental chef bringing us his cooking

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are being worked up, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Japanese chef serves us a dish of his own making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' is the anagram signal for US HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese vinegared-rice dish is a staple of chefs in the Far East.

clue.text: Diamonds — only the very best will do for one's sweet

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
the cream is the best of anything, as in 'the cream of the crop'

explanation.surface: A demanding lover insists that only diamonds of top quality will do for a gift to their sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' is the British word for dessert. 'one's sweet' reads as a sweetheart, but the definition is the pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert is called a sweet in Britain, and this frozen dairy treat is a common one.

clue.text: Note to nurse about a rest

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the word for nurse goes round the letter

parts.note: a minder looks after someone, as a nurse does

explanation.surface: A memo telling a nurse to take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside MINDER, giving MAINDER.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over, the rest, is what remains after the rest is taken.

clue.text: Watch TV programme again over a half of beer

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a repeat is a programme shown again

indicators.note: half of the word is taken, here its second half

explanation.surface: Rewatching a TV show over half a pint of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: A repeater is a pocket watch that chimes the time when a button is pressed. 'a half' sounds like a half-pint; it means half the word's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of timepiece that strikes the last hour and quarter again on demand.

clue.text: Collaborating with governing class

parts.note: the party in power is said to be in
a league is a class or level, as in 'not in the same league'

explanation.surface: Someone colluding with the ruling class.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allied with someone, often secretly, is the same as collaborating with them.

clue.text: It should grip the kids

definitions.meaning: a tool like pincers or pliers that grips

explanation.surface: A thrilling story is supposed to grip the children.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a pincers-like gripping tool, and in British slang small children.

clue.text: State with sea to the east

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea

explanation.surface: A description of a coastal state lying on the ocean to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the sea, as in 'the Spanish Main'.
explanation.definitionFit: The New England state is one of the fifty American states, and it does border the Atlantic to its east.

clue.text: As an alternative, Dante is available in translation

indicators.note: a translation turns the words into something else, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An Italian classic is offered in English versions as a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in translation' signals the anagram of DANTE IS; 'available' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: In place of something else means the same as an alternative.

clue.text: Black man that gets flung off ship

parts.note: jet is a deep black colour
Sam is a man's name

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned sailor thrown overboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods thrown overboard to lighten a vessel are jetsam, as in 'flotsam and jetsam'.

clue.text: Caesar, in bad mood, beheaded soldiers

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: a temper is a fit of bad mood
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar, in a rage, has some of his soldiers executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' takes the T off TEMPER, leaving EMPER. OR (other ranks) is the usual crossword term for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar became the title of Roman rulers, so it stands for a supreme imperial ruler.

clue.text: Stock of it is held as loot

definitions.meaning: a gun is held by its stock, the wooden butt

explanation.surface: Stolen goods are being held in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm held at the stock is one sense; the other is the verb meaning to search and plunder.

clue.text: Bible classes, for example, given to children make fresh impression

parts.note: RE is religious education, school lessons that include Bible study
issue means offspring, a person's children

explanation.surface: Teaching scripture to children leaves a new mark on them.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, religious education, is the British school subject covering religion.
explanation.definitionFit: To print or publish again is to produce a fresh impression, in the printing sense of a new run.

clue.text: Bundle ambassador into nearly secure accommodation

indicators.note: the ambassador's abbreviation goes inside the shortened word
nearly the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a safe is a secure place to keep things
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Someone hustles a diplomat into a safe house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bundle' looks like a verb in the surface, hustling the ambassador, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tied bundle, especially of corn stalks or papers, is the meaning.

clue.text: Fitting for shift

definitions.meaning: suitable or advantageous in the circumstances
a shift is a device or makeshift measure for getting by

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means suitable or convenient; as a noun it is a means or contrivance for a purpose.

clue.text: She needs to listen

parts.note: heard aloud, 'she needs' is 'she kneads', describing a woman who works muscles with her hands

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a woman who must pay attention, but 'to listen' says hear it: 'she kneads'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who gives massages works the muscles by kneading them.

clue.text: Businessman embarrassed by skilful work being rejected

indicators.note: being rejected means the pieces are turned back to front

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red
art is skilful work or craft

explanation.surface: An entrepreneur blushes when his artwork is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rejected' turns RED + ART, giving the whole run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who buys and sells goods is a merchant or dealer, a kind of businessman.
